title: v0.24 Upgrade causing disk space issues on servers
body:
RocksDB garbage collection not clearing disk up after collections marked for deletion.  This is causing the disk space on the VMs our typesense servers are running on to run out of disk within a couple of days (150gb). Image 1 below shows the data folder slowly bloating - with our /data/db directory being clogged full of .sst files (Image 2).

img1
![Capture](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47216699/224299277-20798434-7490-4e90-80d9-5e9d97dff3ef.PNG)

img2
![Capture](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47216699/224301540-7a349841-2b37-47c8-83ed-8d024958f87a.PNG)

Upgrade servers to new v0.24. Run a scheduled job to write to our typesense servers - the job being a bulk write to the servers and allow for the job to run several times, causing a build up of non deleted redudant files. Image 3 shows Time vs Disk space on the VM when upgrading to v0.24 with scheduled jobs writing to our Typesense server. 

Img3
![Capture](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47216699/224310157-5b8b3a6e-01d0-4a3f-a9aa-51c8b04e3f08.PNG)


Expected behaviour is that the RocksDB compaction will kick in on redundant data and permanently remove that data from the disk. As does on v0.23.

Data on the disk continues to ramp up and data directory slowly bloats until it reaches maximum space and bricks the VM. 

Rolling back to v0.23 resolves this issue entirely.

**Typesense Version**:
Typesense v0.24

Worth noting we're running the official typesense docker image.
image: typesense/typesense:0.23.1 - works fine
Image: typesense/typesense:0.24.0 - issue

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
@reporter 

Thank you for reporting this issue.

> Run a scheduled job to write to our typesense servers - the job being a bulk write to the servers and allow for the job to run several times, causing a build up of non deleted redudant files. 

Can you give me some more details on what this scheduled job does exactly? Does it use the import end-point to send the same set of documents over and over again in `upsert` mode?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
@reporter 

I just tried reproducing this issue but could not. Here's what I did:

1. Imported 1M records
2. Checked the size of the data directory
3. Reimported the same 1M records with `action=upsert` mode, but scrambled up the IDs so that each document is treated as an update
4. Measured the size of the data directory

While the data size grew during the reimport step, eventually compaction kicked in and the eventual file size was back to what it was after step 1.

I have a couple of questions:

1. Would it be possible for you to share a similar disk usage graph for 0.23?
2. Would you be able to try this out on a smaller subset of your data to see if it's reproduceable?
